title: local-dev-fastpath-workshop-playbook
summary: A practical short-form workshop that shows a fast local dev loop to validate hosted->dedicated routing, cache warmup, and graceful fallback using a minimal Docker stack and a tiny routing stub.
audience: Solutions engineers, customer developers, and SREs running early POCs who want a reproducible local environment to test routing, cache warmup, and observability signals.
objectives: Stand up a reproducible single-machine demo that mimics hosted -> dedicated fallback
Observe KV cache warmup effects on p50/p95 latency
Implement a basic routing policy that prefers local dedicated but falls back to hosted API
Emit and inspect fallback and cost-related metrics in a lightweight observability stack
prerequisites: Laptop with Docker and Docker Compose installed
Git installed and permission to clone demo repo
agenda: 40m - Hands-on: bring up stack and run sample workload
15m - Modify routing rules and re-run workload
20m - Wrap-up and next steps for customer POC
reference_architecture: Single-machine Docker Compose: router service, dedicated-serving stub (Flask simulating quantized runtime), Redis for KV cache, Prometheus exporter + Grafana dashboard, and a simple load generator. Router decides routing based on health + capacity flag and forwards to local stub or hosted API accordingly.
lab_steps: cp .env.example .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY to your test key
open http://localhost:8080/ui to confirm router and dedicated-stub health
tail router logs: docker-compose logs -f router
force latency/capacity change: edit router/config.yml or use router UI toggle to simulate capacity pressure
run cache warmup: python tools/warmup_cache.py --prefix 'customer-A' --tokens 2000 and re-run loadgen to compare latency metrics
open Prometheus at http://localhost:9090 and Grafana at http://localhost:3000 to inspect demo dashboards
sample_code_snippets:
# docker-compose.yml fragment
version: '3.7'
services:
  router:
    build: ./router
    ports:
      - '8080:8080'
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}
  dedicated:
    build: ./dedicated-stub
    ports:
      - '8081:8081'
  redis:
    image: redis:6-alpine
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus
    ports:
      - '9090:9090'

# tools/warmup_cache.py (usage example)
import requests
for i in range(50):
    prefix = f'customer-A:{i}'
    requests.post('http://localhost:8080/cache/warm', json={'prefix': prefix, 'tokens': 100})
print('warmup done')
observability_guidance: Label requests with routing_decision and model_variant to make routing behavior visible in metrics
Record token_count and raw_latency per request; aggregate to p50/p95 for presentation
Emit a counter fallback_total{reason="capacity"} for each routed fallback event
Expose cache_hit boolean per request so you can compare warmup vs cold runs
troubleshooting: Dedicated stub failing: run docker-compose logs dedicated and rebuild image if errors present
Router always falling back: verify LOCAL_READY toggle in router/config.yml or environment override
No cache hits after warmup: confirm warmup requests reached router and Redis keys exist via redis-cli KEYS '*'
Grafana shows no metrics: check Prometheus scrape configs and that exporters are reachable from Prometheus container
safety_considerations: Use a sandbox or restricted hosted API key; do not use production keys for demos
Do not include customer PII or real secrets in demo warmup payloads; use synthetic text
Throttle loadgen to avoid accidental spikes against external hosted endpoints
post_workshop_action_items: Fork the demo repo and create a customer-specific branch with preseeded prompts and config
Capture baseline p50/p95 numbers for the customer's workload and add to the POC brief
If customer requires private deployment, swap the hosted target to a private deployment stub and add KMS integration steps
notes_to_presenter: If attendee laptops are constrained, reduce loadgen RPS to 5 or run load generator from instructor machine
Keep the demo focused on the routing and cache effects rather than model fidelity
Have screenshots of Grafana dashboards available as a fallback if attendees cannot reach localhost UIs
